missions.title: An apartment viewing time
paragraphs: A renter wants to see an apartment. The suggested viewing overlaps with work. The people involved need enough information to choose a practical response.
The priority is to suggest two alternative viewing times. The expected benefit is that the agent can choose an available time. This gives the response a clear purpose that can be checked afterwards.

It is important to make a realistic commitment. The people involved can identify what they know, ask about anything uncertain, and agree on the next action. This approach is more reliable than giving an immediate answer that has not been checked.

A home affects everyday life, so a quick first impression is not enough. It is useful to ask which costs are included, how repairs are reported, and what arrangements apply to shared areas. Writing down the answers gives you something clear to compare when you look at another place or discuss a problem later.

In a similar conversation, you could say: “What's included in the rent, and what do I pay separately?” “Could we arrange a viewing for Saturday morning?” “When would it be available for someone to move in?”

missions.title: A missing handover owner
paragraphs: A colleague starts a new task during a handover. Nobody has agreed who will answer later questions. The people involved need enough information to choose a practical response.

The priority is to name a contact for follow-up questions. The expected benefit is that the colleague can get clarification when needed. This gives the response a clear purpose that can be checked afterwards.

It is important to make a realistic commitment. The people involved can identify what they know, ask about anything uncertain, and agree on the next action. This approach is more reliable than giving an immediate answer that has not been checked.

A handover should help another person continue without having to guess. It is useful to separate completed work from unfinished work and explain which task needs attention first. Important documents should be easy to find. Before leaving, check that the next person knows who to contact if something is unclear or an unexpected problem appears.
In a similar conversation, you could say: “Where did we leave off before the shift changed?” “Thanks for the update. I'll take it from here.” “Is there anything else I should know before you leave?”
